examples.en: The Far East region is very cold in winter.

examples.ko: 러시아 극동에는 큰 항구 도시가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a large port city in the Russian Far East.

examples.ko: 유럽 사람들은 옛날에 한국과 일본을 극동이라고 불렀어요.
examples.en: In the past, Europeans called Korea and Japan the Far East.
The situation in the Far East often appears in the news.

examples.ko: 극동 쪽으로 가는 비행기는 자리가 많지 않아요.
examples.en: Flights heading to the Far East don't have many seats.
Merchants from the Far East gathered at the market.

explain: 유럽에서 본 동쪽 끝이라는 관점에서 나온 말이라, 요즘은 '동아시아'를 더 많이 써요. 러시아 '극동 지역'처럼 뉴스나 역사 이야기에서 주로 만나요.
explain_en: This word comes from a European viewpoint of the eastern edge, so '동아시아' is used more often today. You mostly meet it in news and history, as in Russia's '극동 지역'.

examples.en: They are looking for the place where the fire started.
I wonder where this rumor came from.
The source of the epidemic has not been identified yet.

examples.ko: 냄새가 나는 근원지로 가 봤더니 냉장고 뒤였어요.
examples.en: I went to where the smell came from, and it was behind the fridge.

examples.ko: 근원지에서 가까울수록 소리가 더 크게 들려요.
examples.en: The closer you are to the source, the louder the sound is.
Residents near the source evacuated first.

explain: 어떤 일이나 물건이 처음 시작된 장소를 말해요. 정보가 어디서 나왔는지는 '출처'라고 하고, 강물 같은 것의 시작은 '발원지'라고 해요. '소문의 근원지', '불의 근원지'처럼 원인이 된 장소에 많이 써요.
explain_en: It means the place where something first started. Where information came from is '출처', and the start of a river is '발원지'. It is often used for the place of origin, as in '소문의 근원지' (rumor's source) or '불의 근원지' (where a fire began).

examples.ko: 거래 내역을 낱낱이 확인했지만 이상한 점은 없었어요.
examples.en: I checked every transaction one by one, but found nothing strange.

examples.ko: 회의 의견을 낱낱이 정리해 주실래요? — 네, 오늘 안에 보낼게요.
examples.en: Could you write up every opinion from the meeting? — Yes, I'll send it today.

examples.ko: 형사는 범인의 움직임을 낱낱이 파악하고 있었어요.
examples.en: The detective had a full grasp of the culprit's every move.
Please tell me the facts in full detail.

examples.ko: 낱낱의 사례를 따져 보면 문제가 달라 보여요.
examples.en: If you examine each individual case, the problem looks different.

examples.ko: 선생님은 틀린 문제를 낱낱이 짚어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher went through each wrong answer one by one.

explain: 대부분 '낱낱이'라는 부사로 써서 '하나도 빼지 않고 전부'라는 느낌을 줘요. '샅샅이'는 구석구석 찾을 때('샅샅이 뒤지다'), '낱낱이'는 사실이나 내용을 하나하나 밝히거나 설명할 때('낱낱이 밝히다') 어울려요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as the adverb '낱낱이', giving the feel of 'every single one, leaving nothing out'. '샅샅이' fits searching every corner ('샅샅이 뒤지다'), while '낱낱이' fits revealing or explaining facts and details one by one ('낱낱이 밝히다').

examples.en: The bride wore a white veil.
Her face was faintly visible through the veil.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 사생활은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
examples.en: That singer's private life is still shrouded in mystery.

examples.ko: 새 게임이 오늘 드디어 베일을 벗어요.
examples.en: The new game finally gets unveiled today.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 어머니가 신부의 베일을 바로잡아 줬어요.
examples.en: At the wedding, her mother straightened the bride's veil.

examples.ko: 창문에 얇은 베일 같은 커튼을 달았어요.
examples.en: I hung a thin, veil-like curtain on the window.

explain: '베일'은 얼굴이나 머리에 쓰는 얇은 천이에요. 결혼식 장면에서 볼 수 있고, 비유로 '아직 공개되지 않은 상태'를 말할 때도 많이 써요. 뉴스에서는 '베일에 싸이다', '베일을 벗다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 회사의 새 계획은 아직 베일에 싸여 있어요.
phrases.en: The company's new plan is still shrouded in mystery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 일의 정체, 내용이 아직 알려지지 않았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the identity or contents of a person or matter are still unknown.

phrases.en: The new phone was unveiled today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감추어 둔 것이 처음 공개될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something kept hidden is revealed for the first time.

explain_en: '베일' is the thin cloth worn over the face or head, often seen at weddings. It is also widely used figuratively for something not yet made public. In news, '베일에 싸이다' and '베일을 벗다' come up often.

examples.en: The press crowded into the accident scene.
The player gave his thoughts in front of the press.
The press's questions went on endlessly.
The police guided the press out of the scene.

examples.ko: 공항에는 보도진 수십 명이 기다리고 있었어요.
examples.en: Dozens of reporters were waiting at the airport.
Photography was not allowed for the press.

explain: 기자들을 한 무리로 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 기자 한 사람은 '기자'라고 하고 '보도진 한 명'이라고는 잘 안 해요. '취재진'도 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It names reporters as a group. For one person you say '기자', and '보도진 한 명' sounds unnatural. '취재진' is a similar word.

examples.en: The package was lost during delivery.
If your card is lost, contact the bank right away.
I found my lost wallet at the police station.
My luggage was lost, so I asked an airport employee.
I made a copy in case the documents got lost.
Many items get lost on the subway.

explain: 분실되다는 물건이 어딘가에서 없어졌다는 말이에요. 내가 잃어버렸을 때는 '잃어버리다'를 쓰고, 분실되다는 택배나 카드처럼 공식적인 상황에서 자주 써요. 같이 쓰는 말은 '분실 신고'예요.
explain_en: 분실되다 means something has gone missing. When you lose something yourself, say 잃어버리다; 분실되다 fits official cases like parcels and cards. A common partner is 분실 신고 (lost report).

examples.ko: 어릴 때 살던 집이 아직도 생생히 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the house I lived in as a child vividly.

examples.ko: 그날 본 장면을 생생히 떠올릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can vividly recall the scene I saw that day.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 옛 시장의 모습을 생생히 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the old market vividly.

examples.ko: 꿈이 너무 생생히 느껴져서 깬 뒤에도 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The dream felt so real that I was startled even after waking up.
My grandfather tells old stories in a vivid way.

examples.ko: 첫 무대에 선 순간의 떨림이 생생히 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The trembling of the moment I first stood on stage is still fresh.

explain: 기억이나 묘사, 느낌이 실제처럼 또렷할 때 써요. '기억나다, 떠오르다, 보여 주다, 전하다'와 잘 어울리고, 말할 때는 '생생하게'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when a memory, description or feeling is as clear as if it were real. It goes well with '기억나다', '떠오르다', '보여 주다' and '전하다', and in speech people also often say '생생하게'.

examples.en: Old fortress walls remain in Seoul.
In the evening I walked slowly along the fortress wall.
From the top of the wall you can see the whole city.

examples.ko: 이 성곽은 삼백 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This fortress wall was built three hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 성곽 길은 사진 찍기 좋은 곳이에요.
examples.en: The wall path is a good place for taking photos.
Tourists climbed up the fortress wall and looked around.

explain: 도시나 궁을 둘러싼 돌담을 말하고, 주로 역사 이야기나 관광 안내에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '성'이나 '성벽'이라고도 해요. 서울 한양도성이나 수원 화성 같은 곳이 유명해요.
explain_en: It is the stone wall around a city or palace, mostly heard in history talk and tourist guides. In daily speech people also say 성 or 성벽. Seoul's 한양도성 and Suwon's 화성 are famous examples.

examples.ko: 요즘 이런 사고 소식이 심심찮게 들려와요.
examples.en: News of accidents like this comes up quite often these days.

examples.ko: 이 동네에서는 연예인을 심심찮게 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: In this neighborhood you can spot celebrities fairly often.
This expression is used fairly often on TV too.

examples.ko: 그 가게 앞에서 줄을 선 사람을 심심찮게 봐요.
examples.en: I quite often see people lining up in front of that store.

examples.ko: 심심찮게 일어나는 일이니까 너무 놀라지 마세요.
examples.en: This happens fairly often, so don't be too surprised.

examples.ko: 해외에서 길을 잃는 일이 심심찮게 생겨요.
examples.en: Getting lost abroad happens fairly often.

explain: 거의 '심심찮게'의 형태로 쓰이고, '드물지 않게, 꽤 자주'라는 느낌을 줘요. '심심하다'와 모양이 비슷하지만 뜻이 달라서 헷갈리기 쉬우니 주의하세요. 뉴스나 기사에서 '심심찮게 볼 수 있다'라는 표현이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the form '심심찮게' and gives the feel of 'not rarely, fairly often'. It looks like '심심하다' (bored) but the meaning is different, so be careful not to mix them up. The phrase '심심찮게 볼 수 있다' often appears in news articles.

examples.ko: 비행기 사고 현장에서 잔해를 수습하고 있어요.
examples.en: They are collecting the wreckage at the site of the plane crash.

examples.ko: 무너진 건물의 잔해 아래에서 사람을 구했어요.
examples.en: They rescued a person from under the debris of the collapsed building.

examples.ko: 불에 탄 집의 잔해가 아직 그대로 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The remains of the burned house are still there as they were.
The road was full of nothing but broken branches.
They say the wreckage of the spacecraft fell into the sea.
Experts marked the location of the wreckage on a map.

explain: '쓰레기'는 버린 물건이고 잔해는 부서지고 남은 것이라서 달라요. 사고나 재해 뉴스에서 '잔해를 치우다', '잔해에서 구조하다'처럼 자주 나와요. 비슷한 '파편'은 작고 날카로운 조각을 말해요.
explain_en: 쓰레기 is something thrown away, while 잔해 is what is left after something was broken, so they differ. In accident and disaster news it appears in phrases like 잔해를 치우다 (clear debris) and 잔해에서 구조하다 (rescue from debris). 파편 is similar but refers to small, sharp fragments.

examples.ko: 저명한 교수님이 우리 학교에서 강연을 해요.
examples.en: A renowned professor gives a lecture at our school.
This hospital has many eminent doctors.
That writer is renowned abroad too.
Renowned scholars gathered in one place.
The painter was not well known, but the paintings were wonderful.
I got very nervous meeting such a prominent person.

explain: '유명하다'는 일상에서 누구에게나 쓰지만, '저명하다'는 학자·작가·의사처럼 사회적으로 인정받는 사람에게 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 말할 때보다 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 보여요. 보통 '저명한 + 사람'처럼 사람 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
explain_en: '유명하다' is for anyone or anything famous in daily talk, while '저명하다' is a formal word for people society respects, such as scholars, writers, and doctors. You see it more in news and writing than in speech. It usually modifies a person: '저명한 + person'.

examples.en: A lot of reporters were crowded at the airport.
The actor said a brief hello in front of the press corps.
The director answered the reporters' questions with a smile.
The press team stayed up all night at the scene.
Press access to the accident site was restricted.

examples.ko: 취재진 덕분에 이 소식이 빨리 알려졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the press team, this news spread quickly.

explain: '기자'는 한 사람을 가리키지만 '취재진'은 기자와 촬영 기사까지 포함한 한 팀이나 무리를 말해요. '-진'은 사람들의 무리를 나타내서 '의료진', '출연진'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '기자' refers to one reporter, but '취재진' means the whole team or group, including camera crews. The suffix '-진' marks a group of people, as in '의료진' and '출연진'.

examples.en: This snack has a high sugar content.
I eat foods with a lot of iron.
I read the vitamin content on the package.
The caffeine content is low, but the taste is strong.

examples.ko: 소금 함량을 줄인 라면이 새로 나왔어요.
examples.en: A new instant noodle with reduced salt content has come out.

examples.ko: 함량이 부족한 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: A product that has too little of the ingredient cannot be sold.

explain: 어떤 성분이 안에 들어 있는 양이에요. 앞에 성분 이름을 붙여서 '설탕 함량', '철분 함량'처럼 쓰고, '함량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'처럼 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '많이 들어 있다'라고 더 자주 말하고, 함량은 제품 설명이나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요.
explain_en: It is the amount of an ingredient contained inside something. Put the ingredient before it, as in '설탕 함량' or '철분 함량', and say '함량이 높다/낮다/많다/적다'. In everyday talk people more often say '많이 들어 있다', while 함량 appears often in product descriptions and news.

en: be contained; be included (as an ingredient)

examples.en: This juice contains vitamins.
Milk contains a lot of calcium.

examples.ko: 이 과자에 설탕이 얼마나 함유됐는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Check how much sugar is in this snack.
It's good to eat food that contains iron.
This cosmetic doesn't contain fragrance.

examples.ko: 몸에 좋은 성분이 함유될수록 가격도 올라가요.
examples.en: The more healthy ingredients it contains, the higher the price goes.

explain: 음식, 화장품, 약의 성분 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '들어 있다'는 입말이고, '함유되어 있다'는 설명서나 광고에서 많이 써요. '~이/가 함유되어 있다' 꼴이 가장 흔해요.
explain_en: Common when talking about ingredients in food, cosmetics, or medicine. '들어 있다' is the spoken version, and '함유되어 있다' is typical on labels and in ads. The pattern '~이/가 함유되어 있다' is by far the most common.
